input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based termination rights (material breach, insolvency, security/SLA/law/IP failures), and Sections 6.2, 19.4 and 27.3 give only remedy-based exits. No provision anywhere lets Customer terminate for convenience, while Section 8.1 locks in a three-year term and Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback. Vendor likewise has no convenience right, which is acceptable to us, so the redline adds a Customer-only right at the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees) as new Section 9.4, expressly overriding the Section 2.1 no-termination language for the terminated Services.

ops.text: Notwithstanding Section 2.1, Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and Customer shall have no further payment or minimum-commitment obligation for the terminated Services. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer-only right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since the Agreement runs three years with no convenience exit at all. Our playbook requires this exit; if helpful we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; confirm no Vendor convenience right.
